schema.name: DMV Vision Testing & Certification
schema.description: Hawaii DMV vision testing and certification for driver's license renewals. Walk-ins welcome, same-day results available at our Kailua office.

mainEntity.name: What vision do I need to pass the Hawaii DMV eye test?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a standard Hawaii driver's license (Class 1, 2, or 3), you must have 20/40 or better in at least one eye — with or without corrective lenses — and a horizontal field of vision of at least 70 degrees in one eye. Commercial licenses require both eyes to individually meet the 20/40 standard, plus color recognition ability.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I fail the DMV vision screening?

acceptedAnswer.text: The DMV will direct you to obtain a Certificate of Eye Examination from a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist. Once we complete and sign the form, you bring it back to your DMV office. Without this certificate, you cannot receive or renew your Hawaii driver's license.

mainEntity.name: How soon can I be seen for a DMV vision exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typically within a few days, and often the same day. Call us at (808) 501-2020 and let us know you have a DMV deadline — we do our best to get you in quickly. We are open Monday through Saturday 10am–6pm and Sunday 10am–3pm at Lau Hala Shops in Kailua.

mainEntity.name: Can you help with out-of-state or military license renewals?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We see patients — especially military families stationed in Hawaii — who need vision clearance for an out-of-state license renewal. Every state has different vision requirements and uses a different form. Dr. Mordue looks up the specific form your state requires and completes it during your visit.

mainEntity.name: Will wearing glasses help me pass the Hawaii DMV vision test?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, yes. Hawaii's vision standard allows corrected acuity — meaning your vision with glasses or contacts counts toward the 20/40 requirement. Your license will carry a restriction requiring you to wear them while driving. We have a full eyewear boutique on-site if you need frames right away.

mainEntity.name: How long is the Hawaii Certificate of Eye Examination valid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The completed Certificate of Eye Examination is valid for six months from the date of your eye examination. You must submit it to the DMV within that window.

mainEntity.name: What should I bring to my DMV vision exam appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring your current glasses or contact lenses if you wear them, your driver's license or state ID, and any paperwork the DMV gave you. If you have vision insurance, bring your card — we will verify your benefits before your visit.

mainEntity.name: Can you handle commercial CDL vision clearance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Dr. Mordue can evaluate and complete the certificate for Class 4 and commercial license holders. Commercial requirements are stricter — 20/40 in each eye separately, binocular acuity, bilateral peripheral field of 70 degrees per eye, and color recognition.

mainEntity.name: What if my vision isn't correctable to 20/40?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Mordue will walk you through your results and options honestly. In some cases, specific restrictions — such as a daylight-only or outside rear-view mirror requirement — may still allow you to drive legally. If driving safely is not achievable, we will help you understand your next steps.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an appointment to shop for frames?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Walk in any time we are open: Monday to Saturday 10am to 6pm, and Sunday 10am to 3pm. If you would like dedicated time with Cory, text us at (808) 501-2020 and we will set a time.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a prescription from a different eye doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Bring a current prescription from any provider and use it for frames and lenses from our boutique. We cut and fit your lenses in our own lab no matter where your exam was done.

mainEntity.name: Can I buy frames without a prescription?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every frame in our boutique is available without a prescription. Choose plano lenses with no correction, readers, or just the frame.

mainEntity.name: Do you have frames for smaller faces or lower nose bridges?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We stock frames in smaller sizes and with lower bridge fits, a real need for many people in Hawaii. Many of our titanium frames also have adjustable nose pads that we shape to your nose, so the frame sits where your lenses need it.

mainEntity.name: Are LINDBERG frames worth it?

acceptedAnswer.text: For many people, yes. LINDBERG frames are made from titanium, weigh very little, and use a screwless hinge with no screws to work loose. Fitted well, they are comfortable enough to forget you are wearing them. The best way to decide is to try one on next to a heavier frame. See our LINDBERG collection.

mainEntity.name: What makes your selection different from a chain optical store?

acceptedAnswer.text: We curate independently. Every brand we carry was chosen because we believe in it, not because of a corporate buying agreement. You will find independent makers, European designers, and heritage brands that chain stores do not carry, and every pair of everyday glasses gets ZEISS lenses cut in our own lab.

mainEntity.name: Can you put new lenses in a frame I already own?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, yes. We check the frame first to make sure it is in good shape and suited to your prescription, then order ZEISS lenses and cut them to fit in our lab. The exception is Maui Jim, which only makes its own prescription lenses.

mainEntity.name: Do you carry prescription sunglasses and sports eyewear?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We carry polarized sunglasses made for Hawaii light, plus sports and safety glasses, and most can be made with your prescription. See our sunglasses.

mainEntity.name: What lenses do you use?

acceptedAnswer.text: We use ZEISS lenses. Each pair is made to order for your prescription, then cut and mounted in our lab. Maui Jim prescription sunglasses are the exception. Maui Jim makes those lenses in its own lab and ships the pair complete. Learn about our ZEISS lens options.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to get my glasses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most glasses are ready in 1 to 2 weeks. ZEISS makes your lenses to order and sends them to us, and we cut, mount, and check them in our lab. Complex prescriptions or specialty lenses can take a little longer, and we will give you a timeline when you order.

mainEntity.name: Can I change or cancel my order after it is placed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Because every pair is made just for you, orders cannot be changed or cancelled once they are placed. That is why we take time with you before you sign, and answer every question first.

mainEntity.name: What if my new glasses do not feel right?

acceptedAnswer.text: Come back and see us. Most issues come down to fit, and adjustments are always free. If it is something else, we will check your measurements and prescription and work out the right fix with you.

mainEntity.name: Do you repair and adjust glasses I bought somewhere else?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and it is always free. Frame adjustments, nose pad replacements, and minor repairs are complimentary no matter where you bought your glasses.

mainEntity.name: Do you accept HSA and FSA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Prescription glasses and lenses are an eligible expense for most HSA and FSA plans. If you are unsure about yours, check with your plan administrator.

mainEntity.name: Do you take vision insurance?

acceptedAnswer.text: We accept UHA. We do not accept VSP or EyeMed, which lets us spend more time with every patient and choose our frames and lenses freely. Some plans reimburse you for out of network purchases, so it is worth checking with yours. See pricing and insurance.

mainEntity.name: How much do glasses cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the frame and lenses you choose. We will always give you the full price before anything is ordered. Exam and service prices are on our pricing page.

mainEntity.name: What forms of payment do you accept?

acceptedAnswer.text: HSA and FSA cards, major credit cards, and yes, Bitcoin.

lens-upgrades-kailua-hi.title: ZEISS Lenses in Kailua, Oahu | Out to See Vision Care
lens-upgrades-kailua-hi.description: For everyday glasses, we only fit ZEISS lenses, including ClearMind progressives. Measured and cut in our own Kailua lab by Cory, our Master Lens Maker.

@graph.name: ZEISS Lenses in Kailua, Oahu
@graph.description: For everyday glasses, we only fit ZEISS lenses, including ClearMind progressives. Measured and cut in our own Kailua lab by Cory, our Master Lens Maker.

@graph.name: ZEISS Prescription Lenses
@graph.description: ZEISS prescription lenses, including ClearMind progressive, single vision and anti fatigue designs, made to order and cut, mounted and checked in our own lab in Kailua, Oahu.

mainEntity.name: Why do you only fit ZEISS?

acceptedAnswer.text: We only fit what we believe is the best, and for everyday glasses that is ZEISS. ZEISS has been making precision optics since 1846, and its lenses are made to order for each prescription. The one exception is prescription sunglasses, where we also offer Maui Jim.

mainEntity.name: What is ZEISS ClearMind?

acceptedAnswer.text: ClearMind is the newest lens design from ZEISS and the one we recommend first. ZEISS built it around how people use their eyes today, moving between phones, screens, and the world around them. It comes in single vision, anti fatigue, and progressive designs.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to get ClearMind?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. ClearMind is our recommendation because it is what we would wear ourselves. If your budget calls for something simpler, we can order other ZEISS lens designs, and we will tell you plainly what you would give up.

mainEntity.name: Are progressive lenses hard to get used to?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people adapt within a few days to a couple of weeks. The lens design and the measurements make the biggest difference, which is why we fit ClearMind and take your measurements with your frame on. If something does not feel right, come back and we will check the fit, the measurements, and the prescription.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a blue light filter?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is optional. There is no evidence that blue light from screens harms your eyes. Some people find screens more comfortable with a filter, especially in the evening, and it does no harm, so we offer it and let you decide.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Gold and Platinum coatings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are ZEISS DuraVision Plus coatings that cut reflections and resist scratches and smudges. Gold is the top performer and has a warm gold reflection. Platinum has a quieter blue sheen. The look is a personal choice, so we show you both in person.

mainEntity.name: Do clear lenses protect my eyes from UV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every clear ZEISS lens we fit has full UV protection, with or without a blue light filter.

mainEntity.name: Which lens material will I get?

acceptedAnswer.text: We choose it for you, based on your prescription and your frame. Stronger prescriptions get thinner, lighter high index lenses. When you need impact resistance, we like Trivex because it is tough and optically sharp.

mainEntity.name: Can you put ZEISS lenses in a frame I already own?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, yes. We check the frame first, then measure, cut, and fit new ZEISS lenses in our lab.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a prescription from another eye doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Bring a current prescription from any provider and we will make your ZEISS lenses from it.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to get my lenses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most glasses are ready in 1 to 2 weeks. ZEISS makes your lenses to order and sends them to us, and we cut, mount, and check them in our lab. Complex prescriptions or specialty lenses can take a little longer, and we will give you a timeline when you order.

mainEntity.name: Do you take walk-ins, or do I need to book an appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Walk-ins are welcome whenever we have availability — but to make sure we can see you the same day and keep your wait short, we recommend booking ahead. Same-day appointments are often available; the fastest way to lock one in is to book online or text us at (808) 501-2020. For browsing the eyewear boutique, frames, sunglasses, repairs, and adjustments, feel free to walk in anytime during business hours.

mainEntity.name: Where are you located and is there parking?

acceptedAnswer.text: We're inside the Lau Hala Shops (the former Macy's building), next door to Maui Brewing Company and directly across from Ulta, at 573 Kailua Road, Suite 106, Kailua, HI 96734. Parking is free — park in the lot behind Lau Hala Shops or in the garage by Longs Drugs. There's a 3-hour limit and a few curbside pickup stalls in front for quick stops. Note: on Thursday afternoons part of the lot is reserved for the farmers market and cars are towed after 2pm.

mainEntity.name: What are your hours?

acceptedAnswer.text: Monday through Saturday: 10am to 6pm. Sunday: 10am to 3pm. Open 7 days a week.

mainEntity.name: Do you see children?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — we see patients of all ages, including young children. Whether it's your child's first eye exam or a school physical update, we keep things calm, fun, and at their pace.

mainEntity.name: What insurance do you accept?

acceptedAnswer.text: We are in-network with TRICARE and UHA. If we're not in-network with your provider, we'll provide everything you need to submit an out-of-network claim and get reimbursed. We also accept FSA/HSA funds, CareCredit financing, all major credit cards, cash, and Bitcoin.

mainEntity.name: Can I get prescription Maui Jim sunglasses here?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We have the most comprehensive Maui Jim prescription sunglass collection in Kailua. Whether it is driving, fishing, golf, or island life, we measure you here and order your pair from Maui Jim. Maui Jim makes its prescription lenses in its own lab, and Cory checks every pair when it arrives. The boutique also carries Tom Ford, Krewe, Moscot, and more at nearly every price point.

mainEntity.name: What brands of frames do you carry?

acceptedAnswer.text: A curated selection including Lindberg, Mykita, Moscot, Krewe, Tom Ford, Shwood, Maui Jim, and others — handmade, high-quality eyewear from designers around the world, in materials like titanium, wood, acetate, even seashell.

mainEntity.name: Do you do glasses adjustments and repairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — adjustments, nose pad replacements, and minor repairs are always complimentary, no matter where you bought your glasses. Stop by anytime during open hours.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer custom sunglasses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — one of our most unique offerings. We turn microplastics and sorted recycled plastics into one-of-a-kind custom sunglass frames you can purchase in store.

mainEntity.name: How long does a comprehensive eye exam take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most comprehensive eye exams take about 45 minutes, depending on any additional testing you might need. We never rush — we reserve a full hour for you.

mainEntity.name: What's included in a comprehensive eye exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every comprehensive exam at Out to See includes visual acuity testing, pupil and eye muscle evaluation, peripheral vision check, digital prescription testing, eye pressure measurement (glaucoma screening), microscope evaluation of the front of the eye, Optomap widefield retinal imaging, OCT scanning of your macula and optic nerve, and corneal topography. No surprise upcharges for premium tests — everything that's standard of care is included. The exam is $150 with your eyeglass prescription included.

mainEntity.name: What if I'm overdue for an exam — is that a problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at all — and no lectures, promise. Whether your last exam was one year ago or somewhere you can't quite remember, we'll meet you where you are. You'll walk out with an up-to-date prescription and a full picture of your eye health.

mainEntity.name: Do you do DMV vision testing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We provide DMV vision testing for Hawaii driver's license renewals — quick and easy, with the paperwork you need. Walk in or schedule online.

mainEntity.name: Are you a licensed optometrist or an ophthalmologist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Out to See is a licensed optometry practice. Dr. Lauren Mordue is a Doctor of Optometry (OD), trained at the New England College of Optometry in Boston, licensed to perform comprehensive eye exams, diagnose and manage most eye conditions, prescribe glasses and contacts, and provide medical eye care for dry eye, infections, and red eyes. For surgical or specialty care (cataracts, LASIK, retinal surgery), she refers you to a trusted ophthalmologist on Oahu and coordinates your care.

mainEntity.name: Do you serve patients from outside Kailua?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely — we proudly serve all of Oahu, with patients driving in from Honolulu, Aiea, Pearl City, Kaneohe, Kapolei, the North Shore, and Marine Corps Base Hawaii.

mainEntity.name: Can I use my prescription from another eye doctor to buy glasses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — bring it in. You don't have to be a patient at Out to See to shop our boutique, and all frames are also available as non-prescription.

mainEntity.name: Can I order contact lenses from you?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Once we have a current contact lens prescription on file, you can order ongoing supplies through us — online via our Buy Contacts page, in store, or by phone.

mainEntity.name: Can I use my HSA or FSA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bring a current prescription, or book a full hour eye exam with Dr. Lauren and choose your sunglasses the same visit.

mainEntity.name: Is dry eye curable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry eye syndrome is typically a chronic condition, which means it is managed rather than cured. That said, managed effectively can mean nearly symptom-free for most patients. Some cases linked to temporary factors, like post-LASIK dryness or a medication side effect, do resolve completely.

mainEntity.name: Can I just use over-the-counter drops and skip the exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: OTC artificial tears provide temporary symptom relief but do not treat the underlying cause of dry eye. If your meibomian glands are blocked, no amount of artificial tears will fix the problem. Using the wrong drops can even make things worse by adding preservatives that irritate already-sensitive eyes.

mainEntity.name: Will dry eye get worse if I don't treat it?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, yes. Untreated dry eye tends to be progressive. Meibomian glands that remain blocked can eventually atrophy permanently. Chronic inflammation on the ocular surface can cause corneal damage over time. The earlier you address dry eye, the more treatment options you have.

mainEntity.name: I wear contacts — does dry eye mean I have to stop wearing them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Many contact lens wearers with dry eye do well with a switch to daily disposable lenses, silicone hydrogel materials, or specialty lenses designed for dry eye. In more severe cases, scleral lenses are often the best solution. We will find an option that keeps you in lenses comfortably.

mainEntity.name: Is my dry eye related to my allergies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry eye and eye allergies share many symptoms — redness, itching, tearing, and light sensitivity — and both conditions can exist at the same time. A thorough evaluation tells us which is which, because the treatment for each is different.

mainEntity.name: Can dry eye actually affect my vision?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The tear film is part of your optical system. When it is unstable, light does not focus properly and your vision fluctuates. Most people notice blurry vision that clears briefly after blinking. In severe cases, surface damage to the cornea can cause more persistent visual changes.

mainEntity.name: My child passed the school vision screening — do they still need an eye exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. School screenings test only basic distance acuity — they miss farsightedness, astigmatism, amblyopia, eye teaming issues, and focusing problems. A comprehensive optometric exam is the only way to get the full picture of your child's vision health.

mainEntity.name: How do you test the eyes of a child who can't read yet?

acceptedAnswer.text: We use objective testing technology that measures the eyes without requiring verbal responses, plus picture-based and symbol charts for young children. We can perform complete, accurate exams on infants and toddlers — no alphabet required.

mainEntity.name: What age should my child have their first eye exam?

acceptedAnswer.text: The American Optometric Association recommends the first exam at 6 months, another at age 3, and again before starting school. After that, annual exams are recommended every year through the school years. If you notice warning signs sooner, schedule an exam right away.

mainEntity.name: Is pediatric eye care covered by insurance in Hawaii?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many vision and medical insurance plans include coverage for children's eye exams. Out to See Vision Care in Kailua, HI accepts a range of plans. Call (808) 501-2020 and we'll verify your child's benefits before the visit.

mainEntity.name: What is amblyopia (lazy eye) and can it be treated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Amblyopia happens when the brain begins to favor one eye over the other, causing the weaker eye's vision to decline. It's one of the most common childhood vision conditions — and highly treatable when caught early. Treatment effectiveness decreases significantly after age 7 to 9, which is why early exams matter so much.

mainEntity.name: Can children wear contact lenses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age alone doesn't determine contact lens readiness — maturity and responsibility are bigger factors. Many kids do great with contacts in their pre-teen or teenage years. We evaluate each child individually and discuss all options, including specialty lenses for myopia management if appropriate.
